correctness.rationale: For every admissible tree, each node has an integer number of children (one, two or four), and level population \(2^ka_k\). Exact blockwise calculation \(KK^*e_v=2^{-2|v|-2}e_v\) determines the complete nonzero singular spectrum, including multiplicities. It gives the sharp Schatten threshold and the uniform \(O(k^{-1})\) comparison of complete and incomplete level sums. Superdominant alternating blocks prove distinct upper and lower logarithmic coefficients; Wold purity with infinite defect multiplicity proves unitary equivalence. The 29,532 exact finite assertions corroborate algebraic examples, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The level-population criterion gives an exact geometric characterization of Connes measurability of this natural depth commutator. It constructs a bounded-local-degree tree with nonmeasurable endpoint and a regular tree with measurable endpoint although the normalized backward coisometries are unitarily equivalent and branching growth rates agree. The precise upper and lower logarithmic spectral limits make this a structural boundary example, not a numerically tiny improvement. Known abstract Tauberian equivalence is fully credited. In the nonmeasurable example the nonbinary branch levels have natural density zero; this provides a sharper structural boundary than simply varying total branching rates.
